publications.title: Attention-enhanced CNN-KAN: a hybrid approach for Arabic handwritten character recognition
publications.summary: Recognising handwritten Arabic characters is difficult because letter shapes change with position and writer. This article combines convolutional feature extraction with Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) layers and adds an attention mechanism, extending the authors' earlier CNN–KAN hybrid for Arabic character recognition. It belongs to a line of co-authored work on making Arabic script more accessible to recognition systems.

publications.title: Location-aware content caching strategy using soft actor-critic for efficient content delivery in software-defined hybrid VLC-mmWave networks
publications.venue: International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems
publications.summary: Indoor edge networks that combine visible-light and millimetre-wave links must decide what content to cache close to moving users. The paper predicts user mobility with a transformer model, models content preferences with neural matrix factorisation, and learns the caching policy with Soft Actor-Critic reinforcement learning. Simulations report gains in cache hit ratio, latency and energy use over existing benchmarks, supporting proactive, personalised caching in software-defined networks.
publications.verification: Crossref record for DOI; open access per OpenAlex

publications.title: MTAGEC: Multi-task Arabic grammatical error correction as a sequence generation with synthetic data
publications.venue: Journal of King Saud University – Computer and Information Sciences
publications.summary: Arabic grammatical error correction suffers from scarce annotated data, and most systems correct errors without explaining them. MTAGEC casts correction, error-type classification, evidence extraction and explanation as one sequence-generation task. A generator builds ExplAGEC, a synthetic corpus of 21.8 million sentence pairs covering 25 error types. Trained Arabic language models (e.g., AraT5) improve correction on the QALB-2014/2015 benchmarks while producing human-readable explanations.

publications.title: A hybrid model for Arabic character recognition using CNN and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs)
publications.summary: This article studies Arabic character recognition with a hybrid architecture that pairs convolutional neural networks, which extract visual features from character images, with Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks, a recent alternative to fully connected layers that learns functions on network edges. It explores whether this pairing is a useful classifier design for Arabic script.

publications.title: Mobility-aware and preference-driven collaborative edge caching in SDN-enabled VLC networks
publications.venue: Journal of Control Engineering and Applied Informatics
publications.summary: Caching by content popularity alone ignores where indoor users move and what they individually prefer. This study predicts user positions with signal-strength multilateration and a BiGRU network, anticipates requests with enhanced collaborative filtering, and places content at visible-light small cells near predicted locations under software-defined control of a VLC/mmWave system. Simulations show higher cache hit ratios and lower retrieval latency than traditional strategies.

publications.title: Collaborative video caching strategy based on delay and energy for software-defined hybrid VLC and mmWave networks
publications.venue: Journal of Control Engineering and Applied Informatics
publications.summary: Edge caching in hybrid visible-light and millimetre-wave networks must balance access delay against energy use with small base-station storage. The paper proposes a software-defined framework in which an LSTM network forecasts user preferences and neighbouring nodes share cached content. It formulates delay and energy minimisation problems and a collaborative caching-placement algorithm; numerical results show reduced delay and energy consumption and higher cache hit rates.

publications.title: Towards improved ship weather routing through multi-objective optimization with high performance computing support
publications.venue: TransNav – International Journal on Marine Navigation and Safety of Sea Transportation
publications.summary: Ship weather routing is naturally a multi-objective problem—voyage time, fuel and safety under changing weather—and metaheuristics that solve it are often too slow for near-real-time use. This paper examines how high-performance computing (CUDA, OpenMP, MPI) can be integrated with multi-objective optimisation for routing, and outlines how parallel architectures can make routing systems more scalable and practical. It sets out the research direction of the author's doctoral work.

publications.title: Terrorism group prediction using feature combination and BiGRU with self-attention mechanism
publications.summary: Attributing an attack to the responsible organisation is a key step in analysing political violence, but historical event records are imbalanced and partly textual. Using the Global Terrorism Database, this work combines DistilBERT text features with highly correlated structured attributes, rebalances classes with SMOTE-Tomek, and classifies 36 groups with a bidirectional GRU plus self-attention (BiGRU-SA). Compared with six classical and four deep-learning models, BiGRU-SA achieved the best reported accuracy (98.68%).
publications.verification: Crossref record for DOI; open access (PeerJ)

This co-authored article investigates bidirectional multi-head attention in neural sequence-to-sequence models for the task, part of the group's research on Arabic grammatical error correction that later led to the multi-task MTAGEC framework.

publications.title: The impact of various factors on the convolutional neural networks model on Arabic handwritten character recognition
publications.venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
publications.summary: Arabic handwriting is cursive and highly variable, and CNN design choices strongly affect recognition quality. This study systematically varies batch size, filter size, the number of convolutional blocks and the layers per block on the AHCD dataset to find an effective configuration. The best setting (batch 64, three blocks of three convolutional layers, 64 filters) reached 97.87% test accuracy, giving practical guidance for configuring CNNs for Arabic script.

publications.title: Terrorism attack classification using machine learning: the effectiveness of using textual features extracted from GTD dataset
publications.summary: Free-text fields in the Global Terrorism Database are often ignored when classifying attacks. This study tests whether they add information: DistilBERT extracts contextual features from the text attributes, which are combined with the dataset's key structured features and passed to several machine-learning classifiers. Across experimental setups, the combined feature set with extreme gradient boosting performed best (98.7% accuracy), showing the value of textual event descriptions for attack-type classification.

publications.title: A study of the effects of textual features on prediction of terrorism attacks in GTD dataset
publications.summary: This first-author study asks whether the textual attributes recorded with each incident in the Global Terrorism Database improve the prediction of attack characteristics when added to structured features. It is the earlier study behind the author's 2024 work on combining text representations with structured event data.

publications.title: Prediction of groups responsible for terrorism attack using tree based models
publications.venue: Proceedings of the 2019 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Science (AICS 2019), Hubei, China
publications.name_note: Published under the earlier name form “Mohammed ALfatih”.
publications.summary: Detailed data on perpetrators are scarce, which makes attributing attacks from historical records hard. Using Global Terrorism Database attributes such as attack type, target, weapon, location and year, this paper trains decision tree, random forest and gradient boosting models to predict the responsible group. Random forest was the most accurate (above 84%) and most precise of the compared models, an early step in the author's research on machine learning for security-event data.
publications.verification: Crossref record for DOI (author listed as Mohammed ALfatih); ORCID record

accepted.title: Hybrid weak supervision and large language model annotation framework for low-resource Sudanese Arabic hate speech detection
accepted.venue: IAENG International Journal of Computer Science
accepted.summary: Sudanese Arabic has almost no annotated resources for detecting harmful language. This work builds a Sudanese Arabic corpus from Telegram and Twitter with a hybrid annotation framework that combines Sudanese-specific weak-supervision rules with large language model labelling, followed by human review by native speakers. It then benchmarks binary and three-class detection with Arabic-specific and multilingual transformers, ensembles and task-adaptation methods, providing a reproducible baseline for a low-resource dialect.
accepted.verification: Author CV of 18 Nov 2026; status confirmed by the author on 22 Nov 2026

accepted.title: Low-resource Arabic dialect classification: evaluating BERT-based and large language models on Sudanese Arabic dialect
accepted.summary: Can general-purpose large language models identify a low-resource dialect as well as fine-tuned encoders? This study compares fine-tuned Arabic BERT-based encoders with zero- and few-shot large language models for identifying Sudanese Arabic, in binary (Sudanese vs. other dialects) and multi-dialect settings. The public experiment code evaluates both families on the same data, showing where dialect-aware fine-tuned encoders remain the stronger choice for a low-resource variety.
